Implement perf findings F3, F10 and F4 from the analyst's report ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/report.md (read those three entries; they give file:line, the measured gains, and the fix). #!/bin/zsh
# Usage: identity.sh — head vs the scratch build with every experiment switched on, both fixtures, canonical JSON.
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis
mkdir -p out
for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
  case $project in
    gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
    chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
  esac
  bin/caliper-head extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache > out/head-$project.json
  SYNTAX_FIX=1 TAIL_FIX=1 SEPARATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bin/caliper-phases extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache > out/fix-$project.json
  SYNTAX_FIX=1 TAIL_FIX=1 SEPARATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 bin/caliper-phases extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache --no-checker > out/fixnc-$project.json
  bin/caliper-head extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache --no-checker > out/headnc-$project.json
  echo "$project checker: $(python3 -I same.py out/head-$project.json out/fix-$project.json)"
  echo "$project no-checker: $(python3 -I same.py out/headnc-$project.json out/fixnc-$project.json)"
  cmp -s out/head-$project.json out/fix-$project.json && echo "$project raw bytes equal" || echo "$project raw bytes differ (stats?)"
done
"""Usage: same.py a.json b.json — byte-compare two canonical outputs with the top-level `stats` set aside."""
import json
import sys


def load(path):
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        doc = json.loads(f.read())
    doc.pop('stats', None)
    return json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')).encode()


a, b = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
print('IDENTICAL' if a == b else 'DIFFERENT', len(a), len(b))
sys.exit(0 if a == b else 1)
#!/bin/zsh
# Usage: ab.sh <runs> <extra-args> <binary>... — interleaved extract --json --quiet --no-cache on gate-large and
# Chakra-only; wall, CPU and peak RSS from /usr/bin/time -l, one line per run. extra-args "" for none.
runs=$1; shift
extra=$1; shift
cd /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis
for i in $(seq $runs); do
  for bin in "$@"; do
    for project in gate-large chakra-only; do
      case $project in
        gate-large) src=../gate-large/src ;;
        chakra-only) src=../checker-default/chakra-only/src ;;
      esac
      out=$(/usr/bin/time -l $bin extract --src $src --json --quiet --no-cache ${=extra} 2>&1 >/dev/null)
      real=$(echo "$out" | awk '/real/ {print $1}')
      rss=$(echo "$out" | awk '/maximum resident/ {printf "%d", $1/1048576}')
      cpu=$(echo "$out" | awk '/real/ {print $3+$5}')
      echo "$project $(basename $bin) ${real}s ${rss}MiB cpu=${cpu}s load=$(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $2}')"
    done
  done
done

340-/// What one merged prop was made from, by identity: the checker's prop, the structural prop of the same name, the
341-/// union a prop without a `parent` writes in the entry's file (a prop with one finds it by itself) and the code
342-/// default, each by address (`0` for none). The first two are shared copies
343-/// (the backend's and the resolver's interners), so the components of a design system that share a prop share its key.
344-type MergeKey = (usize, usize, (usize, usize), usize);

346-/// The props one merge has made, by what they were made from ([`MergeKey`]). A merged prop is a function of those
347-/// inputs and the merge's [`ResolverFacts`] alone, so a prop made from the same ones is the one made before: it skips
348-/// the copy, the reordering and the interning of a type that is often hundreds of members wide. Each entry holds the
349-/// two props its key points at, so neither is freed and its address taken by another prop while the merge runs.
350-#[derive(Default)]
351-struct MergeMemo {
